summary: Shumpei Ueyama worked in philosophy, Japanology, and history/archaeology, having studied at Taihoku High School and Kyoto University. He taught at Kyoto University (assistant professor from 1954, professor from 1968) and served as president of Kyoto City University of Arts.
Shun Hidaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who worked as an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and as a part-time lecturer at Otani University in 2014.

Shun'ei Hirai, a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He had a long career at Komazawa University from 1964, serving as professor and vice president, and later became emeritus professor.
Shun'ei Mori studied Buddhist studies under Shoko Takeuchi. He held posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1990) and Chikushi Jogakuen University, where he was a part-time lecturer in 1995.
Shunei Tsuboi was a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Bukkyo University, with posts attested in 1963 and 1972.

Shunji Hosaka studied at Waseda University and works in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Reitaku University (~1987–2004) and Chuo University (~2004), later lecturing at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and other institutes.
Shunkyo Katsumata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Toyo University and Taisho University (~1957–1985), where he became emeritus professor.
Shunpaku Nakao was a scholar in Buddhist studies who held positions at Shuchiin University as an assistant professor (attested 1963) and later as a professor (attested 1976).

Shunryu Suzuki studied Buddhism under several traditional teachers, at Komazawa University, and at Eihei-ji. He served as abbot at Zoun-in, Rinsō-in, and Sōkō-ji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara Zen Mountain Center.

Shunsho Manabe, a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, studied at Tohoku University. He held positions at Hosen Gakuen College and served as a professor at Shikoku University (attested 2015).
Shunsho Terakawa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held a post at Otani University from circa 1966 to 2000, where he became an emeritus professor.
Shuntaro Kondo completed his PhD at Ryukoku University in 2011 in Buddhist and religious studies. He served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2012).

Shuntaro Matsuyama studied Indology and religious studies at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji. He was a professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design (~1974–1996) and lectured at Kokugakuin, Tama Art University, and Bigakko.

Shunzo Onoda specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning his D.Lit. from Bukkyo University in 1993. He served at Bukkyo University as associate professor (attested 1996) and professor (attested 2005).

Shuyu Kanaoka studied Buddhist studies and Indology at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, where he earned a doctorate in 1962. He served as an assistant professor at Toyo University from circa 1965 to 1992.

Shuyu Sakurai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University from circa 1940 to 1943. He later served as an emeritus professor at Komazawa University, where he held a post from circa 1953 to 1987.
Shwe Zan Aung, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, graduated with a B.A. from the University of Rangoon in 1891. In 1895, he studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw.
Shōkō Kabutogi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from 1932 to 1936. He later served as a professor at Rissho University from circa 1957 to 1982.

Shōren Ihara was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kyushu University, serving as assistant professor (attested 1959–1965), and was a member at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998).

Shōyū Hanayama studied Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1956). He served as vice president at Musashino University (~1968–1995) and chairperson of the Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (~1989–1995).
